source_quote: “Monitoring,“ in the context of Live, means passing a track’s input signal on to the track’s output. Suppose you have set up an audio track to receive its input signal from a guitar. Monitoring then means that the signal from your live guitar playing actually reaches the track’s output, via the track’s device chain. If the track’s output is set to “Main,“ you can hear the guitar signal, processed by whatever effects are used (and delayed by whatever latency the audio hardware interface incurs), over your speakers.
facet_assertion: Monitoring means track input passed to track output.
assessment: Selected public routing role represented; not an output amplitude/timing pass.

assessment: Existing linked mode choices and actual button actions, with type/accepted-control prerequisites retained.

source_quote: The default Auto-monitoring setting does the right thing for most straightforward recording applications: Monitoring is on when the track is armed, but monitoring is inhibited as long as the track is playing clips.
facet_assertion: Default Auto is described in ordinary straightforward-recording prose.
assessment: Reset, original installation, new-track/custom defaults and loaded history remain distinct; not a contradiction or global default.

facet_assertion: Auto passes monitored input when armed in the stated context.
assessment: RML006 supplies genuine input/clip positive contexts; short RC006 is not the only case.

assessment: Requires actually playing nonempty clip and positive input first; no sample floor/deadline.

source_quote: To permanently monitor the track’s input, regardless of whether the track is armed or clips are playing, choose In. This setting effectively turns the track into what is called an “Aux“ on some systems: the track is not used for recording but for bringing in a signal from elsewhere. With this setting, output from the clips is suppressed. An “In“ monitoring setting can be easily recognized even when the In/Out section is hidden by the blue color of the track’s Activator switch.
facet_assertion: In continuously monitors input regardless of arm and clip playback.
assessment: Actual armed/disarmed and stopped/playing matrix already specified in RML006.

source_quote: Monitoring can be turned off altogether by choosing the Off option. This is useful when recording acoustic instruments which are monitored “through the air,“ when using an external mixing console for monitoring or when using an audio hardware interface with a “direct monitoring“ option that bypasses the computer so as to avoid latency. Generally, it is preferable to work with an audio interface that allows for negligible latencies (a few milliseconds). If you are recording into Live with monitoring set to “Off,“ you may want to make the Audio Settings’ Overall Latency adjustment, which is described in the built-in program tutorial on setting up the Audio Settings.
facet_assertion: Off turns off monitoring.
assessment: Off is distinct from recording eligibility; matching independently active input/clip baseline required.

source_quote: When monitoring is set to “In” or “Auto,” the “Keep Monitoring Latency in Recorded Audio” option will be enabled by default. This adjusts the timing of the recording to match what is heard through Live’s monitoring. Generally speaking it is recommended to leave this option enabled when recording software instruments or effects, and to switch it off when recording acoustic instruments or relying on external monitoring. You can right-click on the “In” or “Auto” monitor buttons to manually switch “Keep Monitoring Latency in Record Audio” on or off.
facet_assertion: Keep Monitoring Latency is described enabled by default under In/Auto.
assessment: Role and context already owned; actual initial/new/saved/reset state unresolved. No Off unavailability law is stated.

assessment: Actual RML007 already selects two receivers and uses each button. No new duplicate case, automatic MIDI-output propagation or unselected-track law is implied.

When the In/Out section is expanded, you can press the Delete key to reset the Monitor buttons to the default (“Off” for audio tracks and “Auto” for MIDI tracks), or you can select the Edit menu option “Return to Default.”
facet_assertion: Expanded I/O permits Delete Monitor reset.
assessment: RML008 already focuses intended Monitor, uses non-reset state and avoids track-header Delete; source does not settle complete focus dispatch.
